methodology.summary: median of per-process batch means; dispersion is median absolute deviation (MAD)
methodology.clock: std::time::Instant for Rust; time.perf_counter_ns for Python
methodology.Rust core: CBOR::to_cbor_data() on a CBOR tree parsed before timing; CBOR::try_from_data() on prepared wire bytes
methodology.Python binding: dcbor.dumps(value) includes Python-to-CBOR value conversion; dcbor.loads(prepared_wire) decodes the Python dcbor wire bytes
methodology.shared_inputs: Eight fixtures from benchmarks/fixtures.py; each wire is produced once per worker by the installed Python dcbor package and passed as hex to the Rust process
methodology.correctness_gates: Python loads each prepared wire to the original type-sensitive fixture; Rust parses each wire and requires byte-identical re-encoding; the driver checks the Rust-reported re-encoded wire against the Python wire
methodology.process_boundary: Python worker and native executable startup, CLI parsing, fixture construction, and wire preparation are outside timed regions
methodology.map_key_behavior: Rust CBOR trees are parsed before encoding measurements and hold encoded map-key sort bytes; Python dcbor.dumps converts Python maps during each timed operation, so map tree/cache work differs
methodology.comparison_limit: Paired timings are whole-operation comparisons, not isolated FFI cost; Rust tree construction is excluded while Python value conversion is included
methodology.implementation_order: Fixture and encode/decode order rotate across fresh processes; Python and Rust measurement groups alternate order across repetitions
